text: Since nineteen thirteen, every car has been built on Henry Ford's assembly line. Tesla just broke it up.
The Cybercab is unboxed into three parts. Each built in its own corner of the factory.
The front: a cast aluminum frame. Motor, drivetrain, electronics, fluids.
Body panels: polyurethane, with the color right in it.
So, no paint shop at all.
The back: another casting. Suspension, tailgate, panels.
The middle: the battery pack is the floor.
Seats and trim go straight on top.
Side frames close it in. Then the roof.
Then, the marriage. Front and back join the middle.
And the Hulk, a giant robot, puts it on its wheels for the first time.
Tesla says it's up to half the cost to build. The goal: one Cybercab every ten seconds.
